page: Amazon Web Services m8in.2xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Featuring the x86_64 architecture, the instance is powered by dedicated Intel processors running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The compute configuration consists of 8 virtual CPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 32.0 GB, delivering a consistent 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual CPU.

The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators or local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent storage must be provided via network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes. Network capabilities include a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth designed for network- and EBS-optimized operations. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

The hardware configuration provides dedicated compute resources and high baseline network throughput without allocating budget to unused local storage arrays. The balance of 8 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM fits standard business workloads, including web application servers, containerized microservices, backend API services, and mid-tier database engines.

This architectural profile delivers predictable execution for balanced enterprise workloads, mid-tier databases, API backends, and containerized microservices without the overhead of unused local disk components.
